rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING THE PROVISIONS ON VAGRANCY AND AMENDING THE LAW ON PROSTITUTION AS DEFINED AND PENALIZED IN ARTICLE 202 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: Article 202 of the Revised Penal Code is hereby REPEALED. The following amendment is therefore proposed: Prostitutes - Penalty. - For purposes of this article, MEN and women who, for money or profit, VOLUNTARILY AND habitually indulge in sexual intercourse or lascivious conduct, are deemed to be prostitutes. Any person found guilty OF ENGAGING IN PROSTITUTION AS DEFINED IN THIS ARTICLE shall be punished by DESTIERRO or a fine RANGING FROM 1,000 TO 3,000 PESOS, OR BOTH, IN THE DISCRETION OF THECOURT, and in case of recidivism, by PRISION CORRECCIONAL or a fine ranging from 3,000 TO 5,000 PESOS, or both, in the discretion of the court.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-13

rows.author: C052
rows.title_full: AN ACT CLARIFYING ISSUES ON PARALLEL IMPORTATION AND DISTRIBUTION OF FOOD PRODUCTS AND MEDICINES IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: Importation into, and marketing in the Philippines of food products and medicines shall be allowed, regardless of whether or not the same is covered by any exclusive distributorship agreement between the manufacturer and its exclusive distributor, provided, that the same passes through proper registration with the Bureau of Food and Drugs of the Department of Health, with the Bureau of Customs of the Department of Finance, and with the Department of Trade and Industry.  The Act of importation into, and distribution in the Philippines of food products and medicines by persons or entities other than the exclusive distributor, shall not be considered as an act of unfair competition nor an infringement of the intellectual property rights of thhe latter.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-08-13

rows.author: C052
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A THREE (3)-YEAR DEBT MORATORIUM FOR ALL COMMERCIAL LOANS OF SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES THAT ARE NEARING FORECLOSURE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This measure would allow small and medium-scale enterprises some breathing space for them to survive the crisis our country is facing.  The three-year debt moratorium is expected to abate the burden of these enterprises in order not to close shop and further aggravate the already alarming rate of unemployment. They will not be forced to pay their monthly amortization for a period of three years from the effectivity of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-08-13

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RECOVERY OF FINANCIALLY DISTRESSED ENTERPRISES AND THE RESOLUTION OF THEIR INDEBTEDNESS (corporate)
rows.abstract: "Corporate Recovery Act." This bill represents a comprehensive approach to the complex problems faced by enterprises when they, for whatever reason, can no longer pay their debts as they come due. It combines the creation of substantive rights withrelatively detailed procedural guidelines that move cases through court-supervise d proceedings quickly.  It emphasizes the survival of the enterprise while at the same time keeping paramount the rights of creditors with duly registered liens againstthe enterprise's assets.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-08-13

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING ARTICLE 83 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED BY SECTION 25 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7659 (NON-INFLICTION OF DEATH SENTENCE)
rows.abstract: The proposed amendment reads as follows: Article 83. Suspension of the execution of death sentence- the death sentence shall not be inflicted upon a woman while she is pregnant or within one year after delivery, nor upon any person over seventy years of age.  In this last case, the death sentence shall be commuted the penalty reclusion perpetua the accessory penalties provided in Article 40. In all cases where the death sentence has become final, the records of the case shall be forwarded immediately by the Supreme Court to the Office of the President for possible exercise of the pardoning power, AFTER WHICH NEITHER A MOTION FOR RECONSIDERATION SHALL BE ENTERTAINED NOR ANY RESTRAINING ORDER BE ISSUED IN RELATION THERETO.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE ARCHIPELAGIC BASELINES OF THE PHILIPPINE ARCHIPELAGO TO INCLUDE THE KALAYAAN ISLAND GROUP AND TO CONFORM WITH THE PROVISIONS OF THE UNITED NATIONS CONVENTION ON THE LAW OF THE SEA, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3046,AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5446
rows.abstract: The proposed bill seeks to amend R.A. No. 3046 as amended by R.A. No. 5446 by drawing straight baselines on the outermost points of the outermost islands of the Kalayaan Island Group (KIG) and joining them with the baselines defined under R.A. No.3046, as amended, with some amendments to conform with the criteria set under Article 47 of the Convention on the Law of the Sea.  The establishment of new baseline laws of the Philippines is necessary as it shall serve as basis from which to draw the12 mile territorial sea, the 24 mile contiguous zone and the 200 mile Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) as provided under the UNCLOS (United National Convention on the Law of the Sea).

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CERTAIN BUILDINGS, INSTITUTIONS, ESTABLISHMENTS AND PUBLIC UTILITIES TO RESERVE SUFFICIENT AND SUITABLE PARKING OR SEATING SPACES FOR THE USE OF EXPECTANT MOTHERS
rows.abstract: Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, public and private buildings for public use, educational institutions, airports, sports and recreation centers and complexes, shopping centers or establishments, workplaces, public utilities shall reserve sufficient and suitable parking or seating spaces for the use of expectant mothers.  In case of public transportation, devices such as the prominent display of posters or stickers shall be used to generate public awareness of the rights herein instituted and foster understanding of the special circumstances of expectant mothers. Discrimination against expectant mothers in the carriage or transportation of passengers is hereby declared unlawful.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 2001-08-13

rows.author: D013
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A LEGAL RESEARCH UNIT IN EACH OF THE FIVE (5) DIVISIONS OF THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION (NLRC), AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 213 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: A LEGAL RESEARCH UNIT SHALL BE ESTABLISHED IN EACH OF THE FIVE (5) DIVISIONS OF THE COMMISSION TO PROVIDE LEGAL RESEARCH SERVICE, IN THE PERFORMANCE OF THEIR ADJUDICATORY FUNCTIONS. THE LEGAL RESEARCH UNIT SHALL BE COMPOSED OF COMMISSION ATTORNEYS WHO ARE WELL VERSED IN LABOR LAWS, RULES AND REGULATIONS AND JURISPRUDENCE. THEY SHALL RECEIVE ANNUAL SALARIES AND BE ENTITLED TO THE SAME ALLOWANCES, AND BENEFITS AS THOSE EMPLOYEES FALLING UNDER SALARY GRADE 25.  THERE SHALL BE AS MANY COMMISSION ATTORNEYS AS MAY BE NECESSARY FOR THE EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT OPERATION OF THE COMMISSION BUT IN NO CASE LESS THAN TWO (2) PER COMMISSIONER.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-13

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AS A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT SERVICE ATTACHED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS, FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5173, AS AMENDED, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is with this proposed law that the full potential of the Philippine Coast Guard as a civilian agency would be achieved. The legal and formal transfer of the control and supervision of the unit by force of statute would achieve the full realization of the potential of the PCG as a tool in the assistance of the development of coastlines. It would also increase the PCG's capability as an organization responsive to the ever-changing needs of the maritime community, most especially inthe light of economic globalization, technological innovation in the maritime industry and increase in the demand for safe and capable sea transport. Also, the transfer would increase the economic viability, service efficiency and over-all effectiveeness of the agency responsive to the public need.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06478

rows.author: C029
rows.title_full: THE MAGNA CARTA FOR OLDER PERSONS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to integrate into a national comprehensive plan and delineate the socio-economic and political rights of older persons to empower them that they may retain their dignity as they grow old and to provide for their self-reliance, care and rehabilitation to foster their capacity for a more meaningful and productive aging.  The bill seeks to grant older persons their rights and privileges regarding their employment, education, health, social services, housing, telecommunicati ons accessibility, political and civil rights.

rows.abstract: "SchoolBuilding Program Act of 2001."  The bill seeks to create a comprehensive program which will address the problem of classroom shortage.  A salient feature of this bill is the provision of build-operate-t ransfer, build-lease-tra nsfer, build-transfer, rehabilitate-o perate-transfer , and other contractual arrangements that will allow the use of both government and private funds to finance the construction of needed school buildings, and the creation of an inter-agency committee to formulate and ensure the effective implementation of the program by the Department of Education, Culture and Sports. rows.abstract: This bill classifies "HAZARDOUS OCCUPATIONS" for children, Rationale: R.A. No. 7658 ("Prohibiting the Employment of Children Below 15 years of age in Public and Private Undertakings") has notably failed to cover the need of prohibiting the employment of children in the 15-17 age category from all forms of hazardous and exploitative occupations and activities. This bill seeks to fill the deficiencies.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROHIBIT ELECTED AND APPOINTED PUBLIC OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES, INCLUDING THOSE OF GOVERNMENT-OWNE D AND -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS (GOCCs), AND THEIR SPOUSES FROM ENTERING, PLAYING AND PATRONIZING CASINOS AND OTHER SIMILAR ESTABLISHMENTS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Decency in Public Service Act of 2001." All public officials and employees, including those of government-owne d and controlled corporations (GOCCs), and their spouses, regardless of rank, designation, and status of employment, are hereby prohibited from entering, playing and/or patronizing casinos and other similar establishments whether or not operated by the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation: Provided, however, an exemption to the prohibition for entry shall be provided to publicofficials and/or employees who are conducting official and work-related functions such as, but not limited to the following: (a) police matters; (b) work-related activities for those who are officials and employees of GOCCs; (c) conduct of investigattions and query; and (d) other official functions that may be deemed necessary, Provided, That a written directive to that effect would suffice the entry into the casino. Provided, further, an exemption to the prohibition on entry shall be afforded t
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-13

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXEMPT TO THE MEMBERS OF THE JUDICIARY, INCLUDING THE CHIEF JUSTICE AND THE ASSOCIATE JUSTICES OF THE SUPREME COURT, AND THEIR PERSONNEL FROM THE COVERAGE OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6758, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SALARY STANDARDIZATION LAW
rows.abstract: Rationale: Private law practice is undeniably a lucrative job. There is no wonder why private lawyers all over the country and even internationally get good pay and are in the upper economic strata of society.  The economic returns, however, of those lawyers who by their own free volition preferred to trudge the road to public service in the administration of justice in our society are undeniably very low. From this vantage point, we can see the huge economic disparity that the members of our judicial branch of government and their staff have suffered and forego compared with those in the private practice.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05178

rows.author: C087
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RESET THE MAY 14, 2002 ELECTIONS OF SANGGUNIANG BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN OFFICIALS TO THE SECOND MONDAY OF MAY 2005 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The elections of sangguniang barangay and sangguniang kabataan officials set on May 14, 2002, as provided by law, is hereby postponed and reset to the second Monday of May 2005 and the subsequent barangay elections to be held every five (5) years thereafter. Rationale:  It should be prudent, and practical, to postpone the barangay and kabataang barangay elections next year to 2005, a year after the presidential elections. The amount to be earmarked for the barangay and kabataang barangay elections may then be utilized to complete COMELEC's modernization program, thus ensuring fair and accurate voting and the speedy counting thereof in the elections of our national and local officials.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04456

rows.abstract: Rationale: The transfer of the Philippine Coast Guard will entail the amendment of RA 5173. Under the DOTC, the PCG can concentrate on its functions on Maritime Safety Administration, Maritime Environmental Protection, Maritime Search and Rescue, and Maritime Law Enforcement. The DOTC has proposed an integrated approach to the country's maritime safety and water transportation development program by placing all agencies with relevant functions under one (1) office.

rows.abstract: "Hospital and HEALTH SERVICE ESTABLISHMENTS Licensure Act."  This bill seeks to STRENGTHEN RA NO. 4226 (Hospital Licensure Act) by increasing the penalties of any violation of the Act and by vesting the Bureau of Licensing and Regulation (BLR) withthe authority to hear and decide administrative cases and close down erring hospitals.  It also seeks to allow the BLR to utilize its revenues to improve its capability to carry out its mandate.
